result:
The check was failing for every ordinary user because the privilege was never declared. `VisitSummaryPdfReport.generatePdf` calls `Context.requirePrivilege(VIEW_VISIT_SUMMARY)`, but `config.xml` had no `<privilege>` entry for "App: Can generate a Visit Summary". OpenMRS creates privileges from that declaration, so the privilege did not exist in the database and could not be assigned to any role. Only superuser access got through, and I did not verify that bypass in the OpenMRS core code.

The fix was commit 9fc46c2 ("Declare Visit Summary privilege in config.xml (#31)"), which added the missing declaration. Neither the commit nor the PR text I could read names a ticket, so I have not given a ticket key.

Evidence, best first:

1. `openmrs-module-patientdocuments/omod/src/main/resources/config.xml:55-58`: the privilege declaration added by the fix.
2. `openmrs-module-patientdocuments/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/patientdocuments/reports/VisitSummaryPdfReport.java:88-89`: the summary generation that requires the privilege.
3. `openmrs-module-patientdocuments/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/patientdocuments/common/PatientDocumentsPrivilegeConstants.java:17-18`: the constant holding the privilege name.
4. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-label-printing-app/src/print-visit-summary/print-visit-summary-action-button.component.tsx:35`: the UI gate uses the same privilege name.
5. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-label-printing-app/src/print-visit-summary/print-visit-summary.resource.ts:29`: the client distinguishes a 403 for a missing visit summary privilege.
6. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-label-printing-app/translations/en.json:11`: the "not authorized" message shown to users without the privilege.
7. `openmrs-module-patientdocuments/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/patientdocuments/web/rest/controller/VisitSummaryPdfExportController.java:76`: the controller logs privilege-check failures for the PDF request.
